beats.primary: Something happened, and it is still happening. You did not imagine the weight of it, and you are not the first person to lie awake wondering whether it means something about you.

beats.label: catalog id 95 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Distresser
Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ said: "I asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, which people are most severely tested?'"

He ﷺ said: "The Prophets, then the next best, then the next best. A person is tested according to his religious commitment — if he is firm in his religion, his test is more severe, and if his religion is frail, he is tested according to it."

Trials continue to afflict a person until they leave him walking on the earth with no sin on him." And of the same theme, in the Prophet's ﷺ own words elsewhere: "The greatest reward comes with the greatest trial. And indeed, when Allah loves a people He tests them.
And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him…
O Allah, make whatever harm has befallen me an expiation for my sins and a raising of my ranks.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ مَا أَصَابَنِي مِنْ ضَرٍّ كَفَّارَةً لِذُنُوبِي وَرَفْعًا لِدَرَجَاتِي
beats.transliteration: Allahumma ij'al ma asabani min dharrin kaffaratan lidhunubi wa-raf'an lidarajati

beats.primary: Saʿd asked which people are tested most, and the answer started with the Prophets — not with him, not to make him feel singled out. What is happening to you tonight has a category, and the category is not punishment. It is the shape given to people who are being taken seriously. Ad-Darr is the Name for a hard thing that is going somewhere — and An-Nafi, its pair, is the Name for where.
What conclusion about yourself have you drawn from this? Hold it up against the category it actually belongs to.
Somewhere in you is a ledger you keep against yourself, and every entry is in the same column.

beats.label: catalog id 48 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Just
Allah says: "Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight…"
…while if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.
Read the two halves against each other. The wrong is measured to the atom. The good is not measured at all — it is multiplied. The same sentence is exact in one direction and generous in the other.
And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and in justice…
O Allah, judge between us and our people in truth — You are the best of judges.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ احْكُمْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma uhkum baynana wa bayna qawmina bil-haqq wa anta khayrul-hakimin

beats.primary: You have been bracing for a fair accounting as though fair were the worst thing that could happen to you. Read the sentence again: an atom's weight against you, and a multiplier on everything else. This Name does not make the outcome neutral. It makes it lopsided, and the slope runs toward you.
What have you been counting against yourself that has never been entered against you at all?

You have compared, and measured, and still come up short of something. This is the Name for the one thing that was never in that competition — not the best of a kind, because there is no kind it belongs to.

beats.label: catalog id 74 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Unique

The claim being answered: "But they have attributed to Allah partners - the jinn, while He has created them - and have fabricated for Him sons and daughters without knowledge. Exalted is He and high above what they describe."
The argument: "…How could He have a son when He does not have a companion [i.e., wife],"
and He created all things? And He is, of all things, Knowing.
That is Allah, your Lord; there is no deity except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him…
O One, O Uniquely One, gather my scattered self and unify my purpose for You.
beats.arabic: يَا وَاحِدُ يَا أَحَدُ اجْمَعْ شَمْلِي وَوَحِّدْ قَصْدِي لَكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Wahidu Ya Ahad, ijma' shamli wa wahhid qasdi lak

beats.primary: Nothing shares what He is — not a rival, not a near match, not almost. Al-Wahid — the first Name of your answer — is the reason nothing else has a say over you; this is the reason nothing else is even in the running to be compared to Him.

What comparison have you been carrying today — a version of someone else's life, a standard nobody actually set for you? If nothing is even in the same category as Him, what happens if you let that comparison go?
Something you're sure is over will, one day, actually be over — all of it. This is the Name for who is still there when it is.

beats.label: catalog id 80 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Last
ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said the Prophet ﷺ told him he knew who would be the very last person to leave the Fire, and the last to enter Paradise.
A man comes out of the Fire crawling. Allah says to him: "Go, enter Paradise." He goes — and comes back: "My Lord, I found it full."

It happens twice more. Then Allah says: "Go and enter Paradise — you will have the like of the whole world, and ten times over." The man says, "Are you mocking me…?" The Prophet ﷺ, telling it, laughed until his back teeth showed.
…and the Last…
O Allah, You are the First — nothing before You. You are the Last — nothing after You.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنتَ الْأَوَّلُ فَلَيْسَ قَبْلَكَ شَيْءٌ وَأَنتَ الْآخِرُ فَلَيْسَ بَعْدَكَ شَيْءٌ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma anta'l-Awwalu fa laysa qablaka shay', wa anta'l-Akhiru fa laysa ba'daka shay'

beats.primary: He left the Fire last, and entered Paradise last — after everyone who had gone ahead had stopped looking back for him. Allah had not stopped keeping his place, or His generosity, for the very last turn.
What are you afraid you are too late for? Someone was genuinely last, and his place was still being kept.
You have been talking to Him the way you talk to someone in the room. He is not in the room. That is not distance — it is height.

beats.label: catalog id 52 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Most High

Allah says: "And it is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a partition, or that He sends a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills."
Three ways, and not one of them is face to face. Not because He withdraws — because of what He is. A partition is not a wall between strangers. It is what height requires.
Notice what the sentence is actually about: He does speak. All three are ways of speaking. The elevation does not end the conversation. It shapes it.
…Indeed, He is Most High…
O The Exalted, O The Supremely Exalted, raise my heart above resentment and smallness.
beats.arabic: يَا عَلِيُّ يَا مُتَعَالِي ارْفَعْ قَلْبِي فَوْقَ الضَّغِينَةِ وَالصِّغَارِ
beats.transliteration: Ya 'Aliyyu ya Muta'ali, irfa' qalbi fawqa'd-daghina wa's-sighar

beats.primary: Al-Mutaali is that He is above every account of Him, including this one. Al-Ali is nearer than that, and harder: the height is the reason the address has a shape at all. You are not being kept outside. You are being spoken to in the only form the distance permits — and He chose to speak.
What would change if the quiet you have been reading as absence were the shape of an answer instead?
Before the thing you're carrying today had a name, there was already an answer written for it. This is the Name for what was there first.

beats.label: catalog id 79 english verbatim
beats.primary: The First
At the end of his life, ʿUbadah ibn as-Samit called his son and told him what he had heard the Prophet ﷺ say about the very first thing Allah made.
The first thing Allah created was the Pen. He said to it: Write.
It said: My Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the decrees of everything, until the Hour is established.
He is the First…
O Allah, You are the First — nothing before You. You are the Last — nothing after You.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنتَ الْأَوَّلُ فَلَيْسَ قَبْلَكَ شَيْءٌ وَأَنتَ الْآخِرُ فَلَيْسَ بَعْدَكَ شَيْءٌ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma anta'l-Awwalu fa laysa qablaka shay', wa anta'l-Akhiru fa laysa ba'daka shay'

beats.primary: Before your worry existed, the decree for it was already written — in the first thing He ever made. Al-Akhir, the second Name of your answer, is the One still there after it ends.
What arrived this year that you were certain nobody saw coming?
The thing you cannot stop turning over tonight is genuinely large. It is not large next to everything.

beats.label: catalog id 50 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Magnificent
Allah asks: "And have you seen the water that you drink? Is it you who brought it down from the clouds, or is it We who bring it down?"
And have you seen the fire that you ignite? Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer?
Water and fire — the two most ordinary things in a household. The passage does not argue that He is great. It asks whether you have ever noticed the size of what you use without thinking.
So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
Glory be to my Lord, the Most Magnificent.

Al-Kabeer answers whatever towers over you. Al-Azeem is not a comparison at all — it is the size of what is already in your hands, unnoticed all day. And it is the Name your own duʿā says out loud every time you bow.
Say it once, slowly, the way it is said in rukuʿ. What in your day changes size?
You have been trying to picture how it could possibly work out, and coming up empty. That is a fact about picturing.

beats.label: catalog id 97 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Originator of the Heavens
Allah says: "Originator of the heavens and the earth."
When He decrees a matter, He only says to it: 'Be' — and it is.
No material is named. No process is described. The distance between the decree and the thing is one word wide.
…When He decrees a matter, He only says to it: 'Be' — and it is.
O Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my protector — so forgive me.
beats.arabic: يَا بَدِيعَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَنْتَ وَلِيِّي فَاغْفِرْ لِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Badi'as-samawati wal-ard, anta waliyyi faghfir li

beats.primary: Al-Khaliq makes. Al-Musawwir gives the made thing its particular form. Al-Badi is earlier than either: there was no precedent for the thing to be made from. What you cannot picture is not evidence about what is possible.
What have you ruled out because you could not see the mechanism?
Some part of you has already been written off, and you are the one who wrote it off.

beats.label: catalog id 59 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Resurrector
A people demanded to see Allah outright, and a thunderbolt took them while they were looking on.
Then Allah says: "Then We revived you after your death…"
"…that perhaps you would be grateful." Not as a reward for having repented. The reviving comes first, and the gratitude is what it is for.
…and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves.
O Resurrector, revive my heart as You revive the dead earth with rain.
beats.arabic: يَا بَاعِثُ أَحْيِ قَلْبِي كَمَا تُحْيِي الْأَرْضَ الْمَيْتَةَ بِالْمَطَرِ
beats.transliteration: Ya Ba'ith, ahyi qalbi kama tuhyil-ardal-mayyitata bil-matar

beats.primary: Al-Muhyi gives life. Al-Baith raises what was already gone — and the difference is that nothing has to be salvageable first. The verse never says they deserved it. It says We revived you, and then it says what for.
What have you already buried — not because it died, but because you decided it had?

Something happened that you would never have chosen, and some part of you has been reading it ever since as proof that your life went wrong somewhere. The order things arrive in is not what you think.

beats.label: catalog id 20 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Evolver
Allah says: "No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being."
Read the order of that sentence. The writing came first. Whatever reached you was not improvised, and it did not slip past anyone.
"…in order that you not despair over what has eluded you…" He says why He is telling you. Not so you accept a verdict — so you stop reading the loss as the end of the account.
…the Producer…
beats.source: Qur'an 59:24 (one Name of a three-Name clause)

beats.primary: O Producer, repair what I have broken within myself. Make me whole again with the same precision by which You fashion all of Your creation.
beats.arabic: يَا بَارِئُ أَصْلِحْ مَا أَفْسَدْتُهُ فِي نَفْسِي وَاجْعَلْنِي كَامِلًا بِدِقَّةِ صُنْعِكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Bari', aslih ma afsadtuhu fi nafsi waj'alni kamilan bi-diqqati sun'ik

beats.primary: Al-Jabbar mends what broke; Ash-Shafi heals what still hurts. Al-Bari works one step earlier than either — He brings a thing into being at all, and the register was written before the bringing. So what reached you is not the verdict on your life. It is a line in something still being written.
If the hardest thing in your life was written before it ever arrived, what would you stop having to explain to yourself tonight?
Some nights the fear is the only thing you can name. The goodness that was carrying you the whole time — you find the word for that later.

beats.label: catalog id 85 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Source of Goodness
In Paradise, they will turn to one another, asking what their lives had been like.
One will say: "We used to live in fear, among our own people, of displeasing our Lord."
So Allah favoured us, and protected us from the punishment of the Scorching Fire.
We used to pray to Him: He is the Good…
O Source of Goodness, keep me firm on the grounds of Your goodness. Make my faith steady when the hearts tremble.
beats.arabic: يَا بَرُّ ثَبِّتْنِي عَلَى بِرِّكَ وَاجْعَلْ إِيمَانِي رَاسِخًا حِينَ تَرْتَجِفُ الْقُلُوبُ
beats.transliteration: Ya Barr, thabbitni 'ala birrik waj'al imani rasikhan hina tartajiful-qulub

beats.primary: They didn't call Him al-Barr while they were still afraid. They called Him that once they were safe — looking back at what had been carrying them the whole time.
Look back at a year you only remember as hard. What was carrying you through it that you have still never named?
Everything in you that feels like a secret — Allah is closer to it than you are. This is the Name for what you know is hidden, and He already knows more intimately than you ever will.

beats.label: catalog id 82 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Hidden
Allah says: "We created the human. We know what their soul whispers to them — that secret conversation inside."
And We are closer to them than their jugular vein — closer than anything they know about themselves.
The whispers of your own soul, the things you think no one else could bear to know — He is nearer to all of it than you are. Not watching from outside. Closer than inside.
…and the Hidden…
beats.source: Qur'an 57:3 (one word of a four-Name clause)

beats.primary: You are Al-Dhahir — there is nothing above You. You are Al-Batin — there is nothing closer to me than You.
beats.arabic: أَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَكَ شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الْبَاطِنُ فَلَيْسَ دُونَكَ شَيْءٌ
beats.transliteration: Anta al-Dhahiru fa-laysa fawqaka shay', wa anta al-Batinu fa-laysa dunaka shay'

beats.primary: Al-Batin is not an accusing witness. He is intimacy — the One so close to your hidden self that distance becomes impossible. You do not have to bring your secrets to Him; He is already closer to them than you are.
What is the thing you would say last, if you were saying everything? He already knows it. What is it costing you to keep holding it alone?
You have been keeping score today, as if a better version of you owes Him less and a worse one owes Him more. This is the Name for the debt that was never real.

beats.label: from `collectible_names.json` id 92, verbatim
beats.primary: The Self-Sufficient

beats.label: The line before the two everyone quotes
beats.primary: Abu Dharr carried one long saying of the Prophet ﷺ, in Allah's own words — nine lines, each opening the same way. This is the sixth.

beats.label: Sahih Muslim 2577a
beats.primary: "O My servants, you will not attain harming Me so as to harm Me, and will not attain benefitting Me so as to benefit Me."
Not your best day. Not your worst one. Neither one has ever landed where He is.
O mankind, you are those in need of Allah, while Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy. If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation. And that is not difficult for Allah.

beats.label: catalog id 92, verbatim in full
beats.primary: O Allah, enrich me with Your bounty so that I need no one but You.
There was never a debt. Not one your best days paid down, not one your worst days added to. And knowing that — knowing He loses nothing whichever way today went — He still says: ask anyway.
What have you not asked for because you decided today's version of you had not earned it?
Everything you have loved, you have also at some point failed to hold.

beats.label: catalog id 39 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Preserver
Allah says: "Indeed, it is We who sent down the message…"
"…and indeed, We will be its guardian." Not: We will appoint someone to guard it. Not: it will survive if people are careful enough.
The most exposed thing in the world — a text, held in the memories of a few people, in a desert — and the keeping of it is taken over by the One who sent it down.
…Allah is Guardian over them…
O Preserver, preserve me and preserve those I love.
beats.arabic: يَا حَفِيظُ احْفَظْنِي وَاحْفَظْ لِي مَنْ أُحِبُّ
beats.transliteration: Ya Hafeedh, ihfadhni wa-ihfadh li man uhibb

beats.primary: Ar-Raqeeb watches what happens. Al-Hafeez keeps what would otherwise be lost. The promise in that verse is not about your capacity to protect anything. It is about what happens to a thing after your hands come off it.
Name the one you cannot keep safe. Whose keeping did you think it depended on?
You have been carrying a case nobody will hear. Not a grievance you could prove — just the private certainty that something was done to you and nothing followed.

beats.label: catalog id 47 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Judge
Allah says of a day still coming: "All sovereignty that Day is for Allah; He will judge between them."
Not that justice exists somewhere. Not that it will work out. A verb, with a subject: He will judge. The case is heard. Something follows it.
So they who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the Gardens of Pleasure." That is where the verdict lands for the ones who waited without ever being heard."
Is not Allah the most just of judges?
O Allah, judge between us and our people in truth — You are the best of judges.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ احْكُمْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma uhkum baynana wa bayna qawmina bil-haqq wa anta khayrul-hakimin

beats.primary: The other three Names in this family answer questions about the verdict — how it is calculated, who testifies for you, whether the scale is level. Al-Hakam answers an earlier one: whether it is ever delivered at all. Most of the weight you carry is not unfairness. It is a case still open.
What would you put down tonight if you believed the hearing was scheduled rather than refused?
You have been asking why, and getting nothing back. The absence of an answer is not the absence of a reason.

beats.label: catalog id 26 english verbatim
beats.primary: The All-Wise
Inside the inheritance law — the driest passage in the Qur'an, all fractions and shares — Allah stops and says something else.
Your parents or your children — you know not which of them are nearest to you in benefit.
That is why the shares are fixed and not left to you. Not because your judgement is bad. Because the information you would need is not available to you, and is available to Him.
…And He is the Wise…

There is no god but Allah, the One, having no partner with Him. Allah is the Greatest of the great and all praise is due to Him. Exalted is Allah (He is free from imperfection), the Lord of the worlds, there is no Might and Power but that of Allah, the All-Powerful and the Wise.
beats.arabic: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ كَبِيرًا وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ كَثِيرًا سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ
beats.transliteration: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, Allahu akbaru kabeera, wal-hamdu lillahi katheera, subhanallahi rabbil 'alameen, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil 'Azeezil Hakeem

beats.primary: Al-Aleem is that He knows. Al-Hakeem is what He does with knowing — the ordering that follows from it. The verse does not tell you the reason for your share. It tells you that a reason exists, that it is about benefit, and that you were never in a position to compute it.
What have you been trying to work out that you do not actually have the information for?
Praise, when things are going badly, feels like lying. It is not.

beats.label: catalog id 65 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Praiseworthy
Allah says: "[All] praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth…"
…and to Him belongs [all] praise in the Hereafter.
Both. Praise from inside a world where things break, and praise from inside one where nothing does. The same praise. The verse does not wait for conditions to improve before it becomes true.
…and to Him belongs [all] praise in the Hereafter.
All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all the worlds — abundant, pure, and blessed praise.
beats.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ حَمْدًا كَثِيرًا طَيِّبًا مُبَارَكًا فِيهِ
beats.transliteration: Al-hamdu lillahi Rabbil 'aalameen hamdan katheeran tayyiban mubarakan feeh

beats.primary: Al-Wadud is loved. Al-Hameed is praised — and praise answers what a thing is, not how it has been treating you lately. This Name does not ask you to feel grateful tonight. It says the praise is owed whether or not you can currently produce any.
What would you praise Him for, if you were not allowed to mention yourself?
The thing you did that nobody saw — you have half-decided it did not really happen, because there is no one left who could confirm it.

beats.label: catalog id 55 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Reckoner
Allah says: "And if there is [even] the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth."
Brought forth — from wherever it went when no one was looking. You do not produce it. You are not asked to.
And sufficient are We as accountant." Sufficient: no second opinion, no corroborating witness, no case for you to build."
…Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, an Accountant.
O Allah, judge between us and our people in truth — You are the best of judges.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ احْكُمْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma uhkum baynana wa bayna qawmina bil-haqq wa anta khayrul-hakimin

beats.primary: Al-Muhsi itemises; Al-Haseeb suffices. The difference is who has to do the work. Sufficient as accountant means the reckoning does not wait on your evidence, your memory, or anyone else having been in the room.
If none of it needs a witness, what would you stop rehearsing tonight?
You have been measuring yourself against things that are themselves going to end.

beats.label: catalog id 56 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Majestic
Allah says: "Everyone upon it will perish…"
…and there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.
Two clauses. Everything on one side of them goes. What is named on the other side is not power, and not duration — it is majesty and honour, welded into one phrase.
…Owner of Majesty and Honor.
O Majestic, fill my heart with reverence that draws me near, not fear that drives me away. Let my awe of You refine me until I stand before You humbled, but never disgraced.
beats.arabic: يَا جَلِيلُ امْلَأْ قَلْبِي إِجْلَالًا لَكَ يُقَرِّبُنِي مِنْكَ لَا خَوْفًا يُبْعِدُنِي عَنْكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Jaleel, imla' qalbi ijlalan laka yuqarribuni mink la khawfan yub'iduni 'ank

beats.primary: Al-Azeem resets the scale. Al-Kabeer answers what towers. Al-Jaleel is the word you cannot lift out of that phrase alone: majesty that arrives already carrying honour toward you. Awe that does not cost you your standing.
What have you been standing in awe of that gives you nothing back?
You are not asking to be with everyone. You are asking to be with the two or three people you actually miss. There is an answer to that, and it was given to someone who asked almost nothing.

beats.label: catalog id 91 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Gatherer
A man from the desert came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked, "Messenger of Allah — when will the Hour be?"
What have you prepared for it?" the Prophet ﷺ asked. The man said, "Nothing — except that I love Allah and His Messenger." The Prophet ﷺ said: "You are with whoever you loved.
The Companions asked, "And us too?" "Yes," he said. Anas said: we had never been so glad about anything as we were that day.

The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly — that is the Day of Deprivation. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness — He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.
Our Lord, surely You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
beats.arabic: رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ النَّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ
beats.transliteration: Rabbana innaka jami'un-nasi li-yawmin la rayba fih, innallaha la yukhlifu'l-mi'ad

beats.primary: He hadn't done anything to earn it. He'd only said who he loved. "You are with whoever you loved" — the same promise the duʿā above already makes about the Day nobody doubts.
Say the two or three names. That is the whole requirement.
Whatever is looming over you right now has a size. It also has something it is smaller than.

beats.label: catalog id 53 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Greatest
Allah promises the believers gardens with rivers running beneath them, and good dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence.
Then, inside the same sentence, He says the thing that makes all of that the smaller half: "…but approval from Allah is greater."
Greater than the gardens. The verse sets the highest thing anyone was ever promised beside one word — His being pleased — and tells you which of the two is larger.
…the Grand…
O Greatest, let me feel my smallness before You so that arrogance never fills my heart.
beats.arabic: يَا كَبِيرُ أَشْعِرْنِي بِصِغَرِي أَمَامَكَ حَتَّى لَا يَمْلَأَ قَلْبِي كِبْرٌ
beats.transliteration: Ya Kabeer, ash'irni bisighari amamak hatta la yamla' qalbi kibr

beats.primary: Al-Azeem resets the scale you measure on. Al-Kabeer answers the comparison you are actually running — the thing you are frightened of, held up against Him. That verse performs the comparison once, and it uses Paradise as the smaller term.
Name the thing that is looming. Now say out loud what it is smaller than.
There is a version of you that other people get, and a version only you have seen. You have been managing the gap for years.

beats.label: catalog id 49 english verbatim
beats.primary: The All-Aware
Allah says: "O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another."
Peoples, tribes, families, names — every category anyone has ever used to rank you. The verse says what they are for: recognition. Not ranking.
Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you." One measure, and it is not one anybody can see from outside — including you."
…and the Aware.
O Allah, O Gentle One, be gentle with me in all my affairs.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ يَا لَطِيفُ الْطُفْ بِي فِي أُمُورِي كُلِّهَا
beats.transliteration: Allahumma ya Lateefu, lutf bi fi umuri kulliha

beats.primary: Al-Aleem holds the facts. Al-Khabeer holds what is under them — the motive you did not admit, the effort nobody counted, the reason you did the right thing badly. You do not have to perform for the One who is already inside the account.
What would you stop explaining, if you knew the explaining had never been necessary?
Good news arrived and your first move was to check it for a catch. Some part of you has decided you are not the kind of person good things happen to.

beats.label: catalog id 58 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Glorious
An old man asks how he could possibly have a son. His bones have weakened; his wife has never been able to bear.
The answer comes back with Allah's own words inside it: "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me…'"
"…for I created you before, while you were nothing." The proof He offers is not a miracle somewhere else. It is the man He is speaking to.
Honorable Owner of the Throne
Glory be to my Lord, the Most Magnificent.

Al-Azeem is scale. Al-Majeed is scale that comes close without shrinking to do it. Al-Qadir answers whether He can; this answers whether He would, for someone like you. The proof He gave was not a miracle elsewhere. It was the man He was speaking to.
What have you stopped asking for, because somewhere along the way you decided it was beyond you?
You have been treating kindness you did not earn as a debt, and it has stopped feeling like kindness.

beats.label: catalog id 72 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Noble
Allah says: "And We have certainly honored the children of Adam…"
…and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with definite preference.
Read who is being honoured. Not the righteous among them. Not the ones who asked. The children of Adam — the whole category, before anyone in it had done a thing.
…and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.
O Noble, treat me with a generosity I could never earn, and honor me with Your closeness.
beats.arabic: يَا مَاجِدُ عَامِلْنِي بِسَخَائِكَ الَّذِي لَا أَسْتَحِقُّهُ وَأَكْرِمْنِي بِقُرْبِكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Majid, 'amilni bisakhaikhal-ladhi la astahiqquhu wa-akrimni biqurbik

beats.primary: Al-Kareem gives. Al-Majid is what the giving reveals about its source: nobility that is not diminished by being spent on people who could never repay it. That honouring answers no merit at all. It reports a quality, not a transaction.
What have you been trying to deserve that was already given to the category you belong to?
Something you asked for did not come. Not late — it did not come. And there was no other hand it could have come from instead.

beats.label: catalog id 94 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Withholder
[All] praise is [due] to Allāh, Creator of the heavens and the earth…
…He increases in creation what He wills.
O mankind, remember the favor of Allāh upon you. Is there any creator other than Allāh who provides for you from the heaven and earth? There is no deity except Him…
…and whatever He withholds - none can release it thereafter.
O Withholder, prevent from me everything that distances me from You and give me everything that brings me closer to You.
beats.arabic: يَا مَانِعُ امْنَعْ عَنِّي كُلَّ مَا يُبَاعِدُنِي عَنْكَ وَأَعْطِنِي كُلَّ مَا يُقَرِّبُنِي إِلَيْكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Mani', mna' 'anni kulla ma yuba'iduni 'ank wa-a'tini kulla ma yuqarribuni ilayk

beats.primary: There was no other hand you failed to find. What did not come was never anyone else's to give — only His, and He withheld it.
Name what did not come. Now notice you have stopped looking for who else could have given it.
Everything you're holding up tonight, you're holding up alone — and that is the part that's shaking. There is a Name for what never has to strain.

beats.label: catalog id 63 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Firm
A woman was sitting with 'A'isha, and the Prophet ﷺ asked who she was. 'A'isha told him — and mentioned how much she prayed, barely stopping to rest.
He did not praise it. He said: "Take on only what you are able to sustain — for Allah does not grow weary until you do."
The religion most beloved to him was never the largest effort. It was whatever a person could keep doing.
We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and no weariness even touched Us.
There is no power and no strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Most Magnificent.
beats.arabic: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ
beats.transliteration: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil 'Aliyyil 'Azeem

beats.primary: He told her to do less — not because she was weak, but because He does not tire and she would. What holds is not what pushes hardest. It is what never has to brace.
What are you bracing to hold up all night? Which part of it was ever actually resting on you?
You keep counting how long it has been since you asked. The number only gets bigger.

beats.label: catalog id 78 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Delayer
The Prophet's ﷺ own prayer names it directly: "…and You are the One Who delays them."
Nuh was sent to call his people, plainly, to worship Allah alone.
To worship Allah, fear Him and obey me.
He will forgive you of your sins and delay you for a specified term. Indeed, the time [set by] Allah, when it comes, will not be delayed, if you only knew.
O Allah, make me pleased with what You have allotted me, and bless me in it.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنِي رَاضِيًا بِمَا قَسَمْتَ لِي وَبَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma ij'alni radiyan bima qasamta li wa barik li fihi

beats.primary: Nuh did not tell his people a guess. He told them a term — fixed, not vague, and not his to move either. What you are inside has an edge like that one. It was never unknown to the One who set it.
You have been counting how long it has been. What would you do with tonight if that number had an edge you simply cannot see?
You have been treating one attempt that failed as though it were the only attempt available.

beats.label: catalog id 67 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Originator
Allah says of a day still coming: "The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a sheet for the records."
As We began the first creation, We will repeat it.
Read what that promise is anchored to. Not to your record, and not to the odds. To the fact that He has already begun once — and beginning is the thing He is known for.
…[That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.
O Originator, begin for me a new page and bring me a sincere repentance.
beats.arabic: يَا مُبْدِئُ ابْدَأْ لِي صَفْحَةً جَدِيدَةً وَأَحْدِثْ لِي تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا
beats.transliteration: Ya Mubdi', ibda' li safhatan jadidatan wa-ahdith li tawbatan nasuhan

beats.primary: Al-Khaliq makes. Al-Muid restores what was. Al-Mubdi is the One who starts, and the verse offers the first beginning as security for the next one. Whatever ended did not use up His capacity to begin.
What would you start, if starting were the thing He were known for?
You have been checking on something you cannot actually watch, and the checking has become its own exhaustion.

beats.label: catalog id 18 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Overseer
Allah says of the Book He sent down: "And We have revealed to you the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture — and as a criterion over it."
Two words for what it does. Confirming: it does not erase what came before it. And muhaymin: it stands over that, keeping it, deciding what holds.
That is how the Qur'an uses the word about itself. Not surveillance. Custody with standing — present over a thing, and answerable for it.
…the Overseer…
O Overseer, guard me with Your eye that never sleeps.
beats.arabic: يَا مُهَيْمِنُ احْرُسْنِي بِعَيْنِكَ الَّتِي لَا تَنَامُ
beats.transliteration: Ya Muhaymin, ihrusni bi 'aynikal-lati la tanam

beats.primary: Ar-Raqeeb watches. Al-Hafeez keeps. Al-Muhaymin is over it — with the standing to rule on a thing, not only the attention to notice it. Whatever you have been trying to supervise from underneath already has someone above it.
What have you been standing guard over that was never yours to authorise?
Most of what you did today will not be remembered by anyone, including you. It was still counted.

beats.label: catalog id 66 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Counter
Allah says: "Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and what they left behind…"
"…and all things We have enumerated in a clear register." Not summarised. Not weighed into a total. Enumerated — each thing kept as its own item, on its own line.

Read what is on that list: not only what they put forth, but their traces — what their doing set in motion after they had stopped watching it. You do not have to have seen the effect for it to be entered.
And if you should count the favors of Allāh, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful.
O Counter, do not hold me fully accountable for what You have recorded against me, and pardon me with Your mercy.
beats.arabic: يَا مُحْصِي لَا تُحَاسِبْنِي بِمَا أَحْصَيْتَهُ عَلَيَّ وَاعْفُ عَنِّي بِرَحْمَتِكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Muhsi, la tuhasibni bima ahsaytahu 'alayya wa'fu 'anni birahmatik

beats.primary: Ar-Raqeeb watches, Ash-Shaheed testifies, Al-Aleem knows, Al-Ghafur covers. Al-Muhsi does something narrower than any of them: He itemises. Nothing is rounded off or absorbed into a total — in either direction. That is why this Name's duʿā does not ask for an audit. It asks for mercy on a list you already know is complete.
What did you do today that no one will ever thank you for? It has already been entered. Sit with that before you decide the day was wasted.
You stopped expecting that hope to come back a while ago. Stopped expecting is not the same as gone.

beats.label: catalog id 69, verbatim
beats.primary: The Giver of Life

beats.label: The rain
beats.primary: It is Allah who sends the winds. They stir up clouds, and He spreads them across the sky exactly as He wills, until rain breaks out from within them.

beats.label: The rain
beats.primary: When it falls on His servants, they rejoice at once. Just before, they had been in despair.

beats.label: The rain
beats.primary: "So observe," He says, "the effects of Allah's mercy — how He gives life to the earth after its lifelessness." That same giving, He says next, is what will give life to the dead.

beats.label: excerpt, both ends trimmed — disclosed
beats.primary: …He who has given it life is the Giver of Life to the dead…

beats.label: catalog id 69, verbatim
beats.primary: O Giver of Life, revive my heart with faith and revive the hopes that this world has killed.
beats.arabic: يَا مُحْيِي أَحْيِ قَلْبِي بِالْإِيمَانِ وَأَحْيِ آمَالِي الَّتِي أَمَاتَتْهَا الدُّنْيَا
beats.transliteration: Ya Muhyi, ahyi qalbi bil-iman wa-ahyi amaliyyal-lati amatat-hal-dunya

beats.primary: The proof was never abstract. You have felt it — ground that gave up, green again by morning. If dead land answers to Him every year without a miracle, the part of you that feels finished was never actually outside what He does.
What in you have you written off as finished? You have watched ground do this every spring of your life.
You did everything right and still heard nothing back. Al-Muizz is the answer to who actually decides who rises.

beats.label: catalog id 43 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Bestower of Honor
Charity does not decrease wealth…
…no one forgives another except that Allah increases his honor…
…and no one humbles himself for the sake of Allah except that Allah raises his status.
…You honor whom You will…
O Allah, honor me through obedience to You, and do not humiliate me through disobedience to You.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَعِزَّنِي بِطَاعَتِكَ وَلَا تُذِلَّنِي بِمَعْصِيَتِكَ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma a'izzani bita'atika wa la tudhillani bima'siyatik

beats.primary: Every raising in that sentence starts with someone who let go of something first — a coin, a grudge, their own name in the room. Al-Muizz was never for the person pushing to the front.
What are you holding onto in order to stay where you are? Name what you would have to put down first.
There is a day already fixed for you that you cannot see and cannot move. What you do with the time before it is still yours.

beats.label: catalog id 70, verbatim
beats.primary: The Bringer of Death

beats.label: The angel and Musa
beats.primary: The angel of death was sent to Musa. When he came, Musa struck him, and did not go. The angel returned to his Lord and said: "You sent me to a servant who does not want to die."

beats.label: The angel and Musa
beats.primary: Allah restored his eye, and sent him back with an offer: place your hand on the back of an ox — for every hair beneath it, a year of life. Musa asked, "My Lord, then what?" He said: "Then, death."

beats.label: The angel and Musa
beats.primary: Musa said: "Then, now." He did not take the years. He asked only to be brought near the sacred land — a stone's throw away — and there, close to it, he died.

beats.label: full ayah, sūrah-final
beats.primary: But never will Allāh delay a soul when its time has come. And Allāh is Aware of what you do.

beats.label: catalog id 70, verbatim
beats.primary: O Allah, make my ending good and make the last of my deeds the best of them.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَحْسِنْ خَاتِمَتِي وَاجْعَلْ آخِرَ أَعْمَالِي خَيْرَهَا
beats.transliteration: Allahumma ahsin khatimati waj'al akhira a'mali khayriha

beats.primary: Musa was offered more time, counted out in strands of hair, and he did not take it. What he asked for instead was to be near what was sacred when it came. Not more time. Just better ground to meet it on.
If you could not be given more time, what ground would you want to be standing on instead?
Everyone around you seems to be moving. You are still where you started.

beats.label: catalog id 77 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Expediter
The Prophet ﷺ once asked forgiveness for everything at once — his mistakes, his ignorance, his excess — without picking which ones to name.
O Allah! Forgive my sins of the past which I did openly or secretly, and also of the future.
You are the One Who makes the things go ahead…
O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger… Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
O Allah, make me pleased with what You have allotted me, and bless me in it.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنِي رَاضِيًا بِمَا قَسَمْتَ لِي وَبَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma ij'alni radiyan bima qasamta li wa barik li fihi

beats.primary: The advancing you are watching happen for everyone else was never a contest you could win by asking first. It already has an order — known before you were, and held by the One who named Himself for it.
Who are you watching move ahead of you? What if the order was set before either of you arrived?
You have been running the sum on whether there will be enough, and it keeps coming out short.

beats.label: catalog id 54 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Nourisher
Allah says of the earth: "And He placed on it firmly set mountains over its surface, and He blessed it…"
…and determined therein its sustenance in four days without distinction — for those who ask.
Determined. Measured out and set into the ground before anyone who would need it was on it. The provision was built into the place, not delivered to it afterwards.
…And ever is Allah, over all things, a Keeper.
O Nourisher, sustain me with Your remembrance and nourish my soul with Your nearness.
beats.arabic: يَا مُقِيتُ أَقِتْنِي بِذِكْرِكَ وَأَغْذِ رُوحِي بِقُرْبِكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Muqeet, aqitni bidhikrika wa-aghdhi ruhi biqurbik

beats.primary: Ar-Razzaq hands you the provision. Al-Muqeet set the quantity, and set it into the earth before you arrived on it. The question tonight is not whether there will be enough. It is what was measured in before you got here.
What are you rationing that was apportioned before you arrived?
You have stopped expecting fairness — not because you gave up, but because you have watched how these things go too many times.

beats.label: catalog id 90 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Equitable
Allah says: "And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection…"
Placed — before anyone stands on them. The instrument is set before the first case is called, and it is set by the One who will hear it.
"…so no soul will be treated unjustly at all." Not most souls. Not the ones with someone to speak for them. Not one soul, not at all.
…maintaining [creation] in justice…
O Allah, judge between us and our people in truth — You are the best of judges.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ احْكُمْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْحَاكِمِينَ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma uhkum baynana wa bayna qawmina bil-haqq wa anta khayrul-hakimin

beats.primary: Every other Name in this family acts once a case is already before it. This one acts earlier, on the instrument itself. The scale is level before the first soul steps onto it — so equity is never a favour granted case by case, and never something a better advocate could have won you more of.
Where have you been arguing for a fairness that was never actually in doubt?
Whatever has power over you right now is real. It is not the last word on you.

beats.label: catalog id 76 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Omnipotent
A sūrah that has spent itself listing destroyed nations ends somewhere nobody expects. "Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and rivers…"
…in a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.
That is the last sentence of the sūrah. Not the power that ended those nations. The power that seats someone.
…indeed, We are Perfect in Ability.
O Omnipotent, show Your power in my affairs and make Your strength my fortress.
beats.arabic: يَا مُقْتَدِرُ أَرِنِي قُدْرَتَكَ فِي أَمْرِي وَاجْعَلْ قُوَّتَكَ حِصْنِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Muqtadir, arini qudrataka fi amri waj'al quwwataka hisni

beats.primary: Al-Qadir is that He can. Al-Muqtadir is that He prevails — and the last place the Qur'an sets that word down is not over a ruin. It is beside a seat.
If the power over you is not the final power, what changes about tonight?
The way you appear is not an accident. Every line carries intention.

beats.label: catalog id 21 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Fashioner
It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills." That is what fashioning means. Not that you came out standard. That you were shaped as this particular you."

Allah who made for you the earth a place of settlement and the sky a structure and formed you and perfected your forms..." At the end of it all: perfected forms. The word is not improvement. It is the completion of something already right."
In whatever form He willed has He assembled you." The form itself was willed. Not random. Not default. This particular shape, this particular way of being put together — it was chosen."
It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills… *)
O Fashioner, beautify my character as You have beautified my features. Let what You see within me be more pleasing than what others see of me.
beats.arabic: يَا مُصَوِّرُ جَمِّلْ أَخْلَاقِي كَمَا جَمَّلْتَ خَلْقِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Musawwir, jammil akhlaaqi kama jammalta khalqi

beats.primary: Al-Khaliq creates existence. Al-Musawwir creates the specific — your particular form, your particular face, your particular way. The first is the fact of being; the second is the fact of being *you*.
What would you look like if you stopped trying to hide the form He chose?
Every picture of God you have ever held was too small. That is not a failure of yours. It is the one thing about Him you can be certain of.

beats.label: catalog id 84 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Most Exalted
Allah asks: "Is He [not best] who guides you through the darknesses of the land and sea, and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy?"
The question does not argue with you. It points — at the dark you were led through, at the wind that arrived before the rain did — and then leaves you to answer it yourself.
"…High is Allah above whatever they associate with Him." Above the rivals, and above the descriptions. Whatever you concluded He was from what happened to you, He is higher than that too.
…the Exalted.
O The Exalted, O The Supremely Exalted, raise my heart above resentment and smallness.
beats.arabic: يَا عَلِيُّ يَا مُتَعَالِي ارْفَعْ قَلْبِي فَوْقَ الضَّغِينَةِ وَالصِّغَارِ
beats.transliteration: Ya 'Aliyyu ya Muta'ali, irfa' qalbi fawqa'd-daghina wa's-sighar

beats.primary: Al-Ali is about the form an encounter with Him has to take. Al-Mutaali is the correction that never stops being needed: whatever you have concluded He is, He is already beyond it — this deck's own sentences included. That is not a wall you keep walking into. It is the reason there is always more of Him left to find.
What have you quietly decided about God, based on what happened to you? Hold it loosely tonight.
Something is acting like its claim on you was never in question. Al-Mutakabbir is the answer to who that claim actually belongs to.

beats.label: catalog id 19 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Supreme
Allah made Adam, and told the angels to bow to him. All of them did — except Iblis.
He answered: "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."
The answer came back the same moment: "…it is not for you to be arrogant therein…" He was told to leave — the claim itself was refused, not weighed.
And to Him belongs [all] grandeur within the heavens and the earth…
O Subduer, subdue every stubborn tyrant. O Compeller-Healer, mend my brokenness.
beats.arabic: يَا قَهَّارُ اقْهَرْ كُلَّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ وَيَا جَبَّارُ اجْبُرْ كَسْرِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Qahhar, iqhar kulla jabbarin 'anid, wa Ya Jabbar, ujbur kasri

beats.primary: The first, strongest claim to being bigger than someone else was refused before its owner left the room. Nothing posturing as bigger than you tonight has ever outranked that.
What is acting bigger than you tonight? Name what it was already refused in front of.
Somewhere tonight, someone is certain their position can't be touched. Al-Muzill is why that certainty has always been wrong.

beats.label: catalog id 44 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Humiliator
While Musa was on the mountain, his own people melted down their jewelry into an idol — "a calf, an image having a lowing sound." It could not speak to them, and it could not guide them anywhere.
The Qur'an names exactly what followed: "Indeed, those who took the calf [for worship] will obtain anger from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world…"
"…and thus do We recompense the inventors [of falsehood]." The anger and the loss of standing are named in the same breath as the cause — not as chance.
…You humble whom You will…
O Allah, honor me through obedience to You, and do not humiliate me through disobedience to You.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَعِزَّنِي بِطَاعَتِكَ وَلَا تُذِلَّنِي بِمَعْصِيَتِكَ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma a'izzani bita'atika wa la tudhillani bima'siyatik

beats.primary: The calf could not speak and could not guide — it was never a real source of standing. The sentence that can take a false standing away is the same sentence, same breath, that gives the real one. Al-Muzill does not appear anywhere in the Qur'an without it.
What have you been treating as a real source of standing? Ask it something, and notice what it says back.
You keep bracing for the thing that has decided it can't be stopped. Al-Qahhar is the answer to what actually happens to a stubborn tyrant that comes for you.

beats.label: catalog id 22 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Subduer
Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?
Did He not make their plan into misguidance? And He sent against them birds in flocks,
…striking them with stones of hard clay. And He made them like eaten straw.
And He is the subjugator over His servants…
O Subduer, subdue every stubborn tyrant. O Compeller-Healer, mend my brokenness.
beats.arabic: يَا قَهَّارُ اقْهَرْ كُلَّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ وَيَا جَبَّارُ اجْبُرْ كَسْرِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Qahhar, iqhar kulla jabbarin 'anid, wa Ya Jabbar, ujbur kasri

beats.primary: An army came once for the thing that mattered most, certain nothing could stand in its way. It never arrived. Whatever is marching at you tonight as if it can't be stopped is not the exception to that.
What is marching at you that you have decided cannot be stopped? It would not be the first thing to be certain of that.
Their voices were giving out on the climb, and the Prophet ﷺ stopped them — not to make them louder. To hand them nine quieter words.

beats.label: catalog id 62 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Strong
The Prophet ﷺ and his companions were on a journey. Every rise they climbed and every valley they dropped into, they raised their voices with the takbir.
He came close and said: "Go easy on yourselves — you are not calling on one who is deaf or absent…"

Then he heard one companion, 'Abdullah ibn Qais, saying it under his breath, and said: "Shall I not teach you a sentence which is from the treasures of Paradise? *There is no power and no strength except through Allah.*"
Allah is the One who created you in a state of weakness, then He created strength after weakness, then created weakness and old age after strength…
There is no power and no strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Most Magnificent.
beats.arabic: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ
beats.transliteration: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billahil 'Aliyyil 'Azeem

beats.primary: He wasn't taught to shout louder. He was taught nine quiet words that put all of it back where it already belonged. The strength was never yours on loan, which is why volume added nothing to it. Al-Mateen — the second Name of your answer — is what it is anchored in.
Your voice was never the thing holding it up. Say the nine quiet words instead, and notice what stops needing you.
When too many hands are pulling your life in different directions — advice, expectations, your own competing fears — this is the Name for the one grip underneath all of it that was never divided.

beats.label: catalog id 73 english verbatim
beats.primary: The One
Before the argument, the challenge: "Or have they taken for themselves gods from the earth who resurrect [the dead]?" — rivals with no power to do the one thing that would matter.
Then the demonstration itself: "Had there been within them [i.e., the heavens and earth] gods besides Allah, they both would have been ruined."
So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
…And Allah has said, 'Do not take for yourselves two deities. He [i.e., Allah] is but one God…'
O One, O Uniquely One, gather my scattered self and unify my purpose for You.
beats.arabic: يَا وَاحِدُ يَا أَحَدُ اجْمَعْ شَمْلِي وَوَحِّدْ قَصْدِي لَكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Wahidu Ya Ahad, ijma' shamli wa wahhid qasdi lak

beats.primary: If there had been a second, the world you're standing in would not have held together. It did. Whatever is holding your life together right now is not divided between rivals — it answers to One. Al-Ahad — the second Name of your answer — is why that One has no equal to be compared against.

Where in your life right now do you keep negotiating with something as if it had a real vote? What would this week look like if you stopped treating it like a rival for control, and let it be what it actually is — nothing?
You have been circling the same spot, and calling it stuck. This is the Name for what happens when you are found there.

beats.label: catalog id 71 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Finder
Your Lord has not taken leave of you, [O Muḥammad], nor has He detested [you].
And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life].
And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied.
And He found you lost…
O Finder, find a way out for me from what I am in, and do not leave me to myself.
beats.arabic: يَا وَاجِدُ أَوْجِدْ لِي مَخْرَجًا مِمَّا أَنَا فِيهِ وَلَا تَكِلْنِي إِلَى نَفْسِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Wajid, awjid li makhrajam mimma ana fih wa la takilni ila nafsi

beats.primary: He did not wait to be searched for. Before anything was worked out, He had already found what was lost.
You have been calling it stuck. What changes if it is the place you were found, rather than the place you failed to leave?
You have been holding a situation together by attention alone, as though letting go of it would let it fall.

beats.label: catalog id 83 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Governor
Allah says: "Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne…"
…arranging the matter [of His creation].
One phrase, present tense, with no object named. Not arranged, once, long ago. Arranging — continuously, all of it, now, including the part you are lying awake about.
…And there is not for them besides Him any patron.
O Governor, be my protector when the world drifts away. Guard me with the grip that never slips and guide me gently through what I do not understand.
beats.arabic: يَا وَالِي كُنْ لِي وَلِيًّا حِينَ يَبْتَعِدُ الدُّنْيَا عَنِّي وَتَوَلَّ أَمْرِي كُلَّهُ
beats.transliteration: Ya Wali, kun li waliyyan hina yabtab'idud-dunya 'anni wa-tawalla amri kullahu

beats.primary: Al-Waliyy is the ally who is on your side. Al-Wali is the One running the place, and the difference matters at three in the morning: you are not asking to be defended. You are asking whether anybody is at the controls.
What are you supervising tonight that is already being administered?

Something is already working in your favour tonight, in a place you have not thought to look. That is not a guess about your circumstances — it is the shape of a sentence the Prophet ﷺ taught a young companion, word for word.

beats.label: catalog id 96 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Benefiter

Ibn ʿAbbās, a young companion, was riding behind the Prophet ﷺ one day. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Young man, I will teach you some words: be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him in front of you."
When you ask, ask Allah. And when you seek help, seek help from Allah.

And know: if the whole creation gathered together to benefit you with something, they could not benefit you except with something Allah had already written for you. And if they gathered to harm you with something, they could not harm you except with something Allah had already written against you. The pens are lifted, and the pages are dry.
…and the [great] ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah has sent down from the heavens of rain, giving life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness…
O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, pure provision, and accepted deeds.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا وَعَمَلًا مُتَقَبَّلًا
beats.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'an wa rizqan tayyiban wa 'amalan mutaqabbalan

beats.primary: Every person who has ever wanted to help you was still limited to what was already written for you to receive. That is not a small circle of people. It is the entire creation, and it was never enough on its own — and it was never the whole story either.
Whose help have you been waiting on tonight? Notice how small a part of the story their yes or no actually is.
You cannot see where this is going, and you have begun to suspect that means it is not going anywhere.

beats.label: catalog id 99 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Guide to Right Path
Allah says: "…but Allah has endeared to you the faith and has made it pleasing in your hearts…"
…and has made hateful to you disbelief, defiance and disobedience. Those are the [rightly] guided.

Read what He actually did. Not a sign put in front of you — three changes made inside you: what you love, what looks beautiful to you, what you cannot stomach. The guidance is not a direction you were shown. It is a taste you were given.
It guides to the right course…
O Guide to the Right Path, inspire my guidance and protect me from the evil of my own self.
beats.arabic: يَا رَشِيدُ أَلْهِمْنِي رُشْدِي وَقِنِي شَرَّ نَفْسِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Rasheed, alhimni rushdi wa qini sharra nafsi

beats.primary: Al-Hadi shows you the way and you walk it. Ar-Rasheed is the arrangement you never see — the sun moved while they slept. Not being able to see where this goes is not evidence that nobody is steering it.
What has already been arranged around you that you were not awake for?
You have been waiting so long that you have started to read the waiting itself as the answer.

beats.label: catalog id 32 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Patient
Allah says: "He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day…"
"…the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count." Of those which you count. The sentence stops to name whose clock is being used, and it is not His.
Notice that nothing in it is late. A matter goes down, is arranged, comes back up — on time, at full speed, on a scale where a thousand of your years is one of His days.
…And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count.
O Allah, I ask You for patience and I seek refuge in You from anxiety and distress.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الصَّبْرَ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْجَزَعِ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma inni as'alukas-sabra wa a'udhu bika minal-jaza'

beats.primary: Al-Haleem is restraint: power held back from what it could rightly do. As-Sabur is not restraint at all — it is scale. He is not withholding from you. He is not on your clock, and the silence you have been reading as refusal is a matter still ascending.
How long have you actually been waiting? Put the number next to the one in the verse.
The part of it nobody else was there for is the part you have started to doubt yourself.

beats.label: catalog id 60 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Witness
Allah says of what He revealed: "But Allah bears witness to that which He has revealed to you. He has sent it down with His knowledge…"
Not that He knows it. That He testifies to it. The verb is the one used in a court, and the One using it is Allah.
"…and the angels bear witness as well. And sufficient is Allah as Witness." Sufficient — the testimony does not need a second signature.
…And sufficient is Allah as Witness.
O All-Seeing, You see what no one else sees. Bear witness for me in what only You know.
beats.arabic: يَا بَصِيرُ أَنْتَ تَرَى مَا لَا يَرَى أَحَدٌ فَاشْهَدْ لِي بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُهُ سِوَاكَ
beats.transliteration: Ya Basir, anta tara ma la yara ahad, fashhadli bima la ya'lamuhu siwak

beats.primary: Al-Baseer sees it. Ar-Raqeeb watches it. Ash-Shaheed is the One who will say what He saw. That distinction is the whole reason this Name's duʿā asks Him not to look but to speak — and it is why the thing no one else attended still has a witness who can be called.
What is the thing no one was there for? You are not the only one who knows it happened.
You have done things whose cost nobody could see. That is the part you assume did not count.

beats.label: catalog id 28 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Most Appreciative
Allah describes people who give "secretly and publicly", and says they can expect "a transaction that will never perish" —
That He may give them in full their rewards and increase for them of His bounty.
Read the order. In full — and then increased. The full amount was already everything that was owed. The increase is not payment. It is appreciation.
…Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.
O Most Appreciative, appreciate my striving and do not abandon me.
beats.arabic: يَا شَكُورُ اشْكُرْ لِي سَعْيِي وَلَا تَخْذُلْنِي
beats.transliteration: Ya Shakuru ushkur li sa'yi wa la takhdhulni

beats.primary: Al-Kareem gives before you ask. Ash-Shakur answers what you already did, and answers it out of proportion. The word in the verse is not a reward; it is a Name. The smallness of what you managed is not something He is politely overlooking.
What did you do that cost you something no one else could see?
In the middle of your ordinary day, you are standing inside an answer you don't know you're seeing yet. This is the Name for what is already manifest, waiting for you to catch up.

beats.label: catalog id 81 english verbatim
beats.primary: The Manifest
Allah says: "We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them — it is the truth."
He shows signs in what you see: the ordered sky, the turning earth, the architecture of a living thing. But the Qur'an says He is also showing signs in you.

The signs in your own self — the conscience that accuses you, the mercy you cannot explain, the reason you cannot ignore — these are His speech. He keeps showing until the moment you know: *this is true.
…and the Manifest…
beats.source: Qur'an 57:3 (one word of a four-Name clause)

beats.primary: You are Al-Dhahir — there is nothing above You. You are Al-Batin — there is nothing closer to me than You.
beats.arabic: أَنْتَ الظَّاهِرُ فَلَيْسَ فَوْقَكَ شَيْءٌ وَأَنْتَ الْبَاطِنُ فَلَيْسَ دُونَكَ شَيْءٌ
beats.transliteration: Anta al-Dhahiru fa-laysa fawqaka shay', wa anta al-Batinu fa-laysa dunaka shay'

beats.primary: Az-Zahir is not a Name for knowledge you achieve. It is a Name for what is *already laid out in front of you — in every direction outside, and in the deepest part inside — and you have not seen it yet only because you have not looked. He is the One who keeps showing. You have only to receive.
Name one thing you saw today and walked past without stopping. What would change if you let yourself believe it was addressed to you?
You want to be near something vast without being flattened by it. Those two do not usually arrive together.

beats.label: catalog id 89 english verbatim
beats.primary: Lord of Majesty and Bounty
Sūrat ar-Rahman asks one question again and again: which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
Then it stops asking. Its final line is not a question.
Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor." The sūrah of favours closes by naming the One who gave them — with both words at once."
Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.
O Lord of Majesty and Bounty, protect us from the Fire and grant us the nearness of Your generosity.
beats.arabic: يَا ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ أَجِرْنَا مِنَ النَّارِ

beats.primary: Al-Jaleel takes the first word of this phrase from an earlier āyah. This Name is the phrase entire, and the conjunction is the point. Majesty by itself would be a reason to keep back. Honour by itself would be warmth without weight. The Qur'an never separates them, and neither does the Name.
Where have you been choosing between being safe and being close?
Everything you call yours arrived, and will leave. That is not a threat being made to you. It is how the ownership was always arranged.

beats.label: catalog id 88 english verbatim
beats.primary: Owner of Sovereignty
Allah opens the sūrah: "Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allah."
Every single thing named there is doing something — exalting, running, existing. Not one of them is described as owning anything.
The owning is stated separately, in its own clause, with one holder. Your grip on what you have is real. It is also a loan you are administering.
…To Him belongs dominion…
O Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and take it from whom You will. Teach me that nothing I hold is truly mine.
beats.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ وَتَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشَاءُ
beats.transliteration: Allahumma Malikal-Mulk, tu'til-mulka man tasha' wa tanzi'ul-mulka mimman tasha'

beats.primary: Al-Malik is the King — the One who rules. Malik-ul-Mulk is narrower: not the ruler of a kingdom but the owner of kingship itself, including whatever share of it you are currently holding and afraid to lose.
Name the thing you are most afraid of losing. On whose account is it actually held?
